correctness.rationale: The finite Jacobson radical is nilpotent and the quotient has no nonzero nilpotents, yielding nilpotent iff in radical. Uniform quotient fibers and independent field coordinates prove the exact formula. Inclusion–exclusion isolates the unique dominant base and its multiplicity, giving a terminating exact inverse. Nonzero Vandermonde determinant proves finite prefix sufficiency; elementary sum/product algebra proves sharp length two for at most two factors. Exact ring-product and spectral checkers both returned VERIFY_OK.

value.rationale: The two-factor NPP invariant admits the documented 15/64 collision, motivating how many word lengths recover underlying information. The converse theorem completely classifies the entire nilpotent-word probability invariant by commutative semisimple quotient, gives explicit finite recognition bounds, and proves a sharp short boundary. The theorem applies to noncommutative radical extensions and makes clear what cannot be recovered; it is not claimed as a new computation of elementary forward field probabilities.
